blocking_findings.summary: Runtime Stage 04B trace and lifecycle metadata identifies Attempt 1 while the reviewed and potentially accepted implementation chain is Attempt 2.
evidence: agents/research_agent.py defines _TRACE_IDENTITY with attempt=1 and _trace_identity_from_state also calls forecast_trace_metadata with attempt=1.

tools/research_tools/__init__.py compact_lifecycle calls forecast_trace_metadata with attempt=1, so provider, SEC, Vector, Graph, Hybrid, comprehensive-analysis and leakage-gate lifecycle records are misattributed.
tools/research_tools/context_synthesizer.py uses attempt=1 in synthesis trace inputs, decorator metadata and compact lifecycle output.

The control plane is ACTIVE at Stage 04B revision 1 attempt 2 in REVIEW, and control-plane.md requires Observability, Primary final, QA and Reviewer evidence for the same stage/revision/attempt. The mismatch makes accepted-attempt operational provenance false even though the product bytes originated in Attempt 1 and were revalidated in Attempt 2.
blocking_findings.impact: Telemetry cannot be reliably joined to the accepted Stage 04B attempt and would incorrectly attribute future production research executions to the failed Attempt 1 evidence chain.
blocking_findings.required_rework: In a new attempt, make the Stage 04B trace/lifecycle identity derive from one explicit versioned implementation identity whose attempt matches the attempt eligible for acceptance; update privacy-safe observability tests to assert stage=04B, stage_revision=1 and the current accepted-candidate attempt across agent, synthesis, provider and leakage-gate metadata. Re-run the full same-attempt Primary -> Observability -> Primary final -> QA -> Review chain.

Historical and provider boundaries are supported by deterministic offline fixtures and mocks. No live/provider test should be run without separate authorization.
